requirements.description: Annual SG&A, net sales, industrial-firm sample codes, and firm-year identifiers from the study’s Compustat 1999 PST/full-coverage files.

required_coverage.population: Industrial firms from the 1999 Compustat PST and full-coverage files, for the 1979–1998 analysis sample.
required_coverage.detail: Raw input begins in 1978 for prior-year SG&A/sales at the first 1979 observation; the original sample vintage/population is not confirmed.

routes.mapping_notes: The live current dataset has xsga and sale fields, but the source defines annual Compustat #189 and #12 in its 1999 PST/full-coverage data. Historical item-number-to-mnemonic correspondence is not established by name resemblance.
routes.coverage_notes: Required annual history is 1978–1998 because both dependent and independent variables compare t with t−1; 1999 PST/full-coverage population is not confirmed.

requirements.unresolved_reason: Current exact columns do not verify the historical Compustat #189/#12 crosswalk or coverage/population equivalence to the Compustat 1999 files.

variable_coverage.construction: Natural logarithm of firm i’s current annual SG&A costs divided by its preceding-year SG&A costs; annual SG&A is Compustat item #189. Formula: log(SG&A_{i,t} / SG&A_{i,t-1}). The paper specifies historical Compustat item #189/#12; current xsga/sale fields are candidates, not verified historical crosswalks.

Natural logarithm of firm i’s current annual net sales revenue divided by preceding-year net sales revenue; annual net sales revenue is Compustat item #12 and is used as an imperfect proxy for sales volume. Formula: log(Revenue_{i,t} / Revenue_{i,t-1}). The paper specifies historical Compustat item #189/#12; current xsga/sale fields are candidates, not verified historical crosswalks.

Interaction of the decrease indicator and the current-to-preceding-year log net-sales ratio. Decrease Dummy equals 1 when firm i’s sales revenue in period t is less than in t−1, and 0 otherwise; it is not included as a standalone RHS term. Formula: 1[Revenue_{i,t} < Revenue_{i,t-1}] × log(Revenue_{i,t} / Revenue_{i,t-1}). The paper specifies historical Compustat item #189/#12; current xsga/sale fields are candidates, not verified historical crosswalks.

design_coverage.reason: Sample is industrial firms from Compustat 1999 PST and full-coverage data, 1979–1998; exact industrial screen and local population coverage are not established.
Firm-year panel identity is required for t and t−1 values and the reported firm-level autocorrelation check.
The selected result is the pooled Model (I); the reported separate fixed-effects result is outside the assigned baseline scope.
The paper reports t-statistics but does not identify a standard-error/covariance procedure for this table.
No estimation weights are reported for the pooled OLS fit.
Model (I) is estimated by pooled OLS.
The source screens missing current/prior SG&A and sales, drops SG&A greater than sales, and trims the top and bottom 0.5% of any model variable.

implementation_issues.description: The study uses annual Compustat item #189 for SG&A and #12 for net sales in the 1999 PST/full-coverage files. The current xsga/sale mnemonics are candidates only; no verified historical item-number crosswalk is available.
Table 2 reports t-statistics but does not identify the standard-error procedure; the White and firm-by-firm Durbin–Watson diagnostics do not establish how table t-statistics were calculated.
The term “industrial firms” is not operationalized with an exact industry-code rule in the assigned source extraction; current SIC descriptors do not prove the 1999 selection rule.
The assigned sample is specifically drawn from Compustat 1999 PST and full-coverage files. Current local data are not confirmed to reproduce that historical population/vintage.

evidence.description: Exact-resource COMP.FUNDA probe verifies current field presence including xsga, sale, industrial descriptors and firm-year keys.
Catalog labels identify current xsga as SG&A and sale as Sales/Turnover, but the paper specifies historical Compustat item numbers.

evidence.quote: The primary variables used in our analysis are SG&A costs (annual Compustat #189) and net sales revenue (annual Compustat #12).
evidence.description: Historical Compustat item numbers and variable roles.

evidence.quote: Data were drawn for all firms included in the PST (primary, supplementary, and tertiary) and full-coverage files of Compustat 1999.
The data set includes annual data for industrial firms covering the 20 years from 1979 to 1998.
We eliminated extreme observations from the estimation by excluding an observation if the value of any variable was in the top or bottom 0.5% of its distribution
We present the results of estimating model (I) for the pooled sample in table 2.

The Durbin-Watson [1951] test statistic revealed significant (at the 5% level) positive autocorrelation for less than 3% of the firms, indicating that it was not necessary to correct for serial correlation in the data.
evidence.description: Serial-correlation diagnostics do not specify the t-statistic standard errors.

evidence.quote: We use sales revenue as an imperfect proxy for sales volume because sales volume is not directly observable.
The interaction variable, Decrease Dummy, takes the value of 1 when sales revenue decreases between periods t - 1 and t, and 0 otherwise.
Decrease Dummyi,t takes a value of 1 when revenue of firm i for period t is less than that in the preceding period.

review_notes: The result-set scope is the one-year pooled Model (I) in Table 2; separate fixed-effects and multiyear variants are not added.
Coverage remains unconfirmed for the 1978 lag input and the 1999 Compustat population.
